To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) folate deficiency induces an oxidative stress in adult rats that is associated with increased homocysteinaemia and decreased antioxidant capacity in plasma; (ii) this oxidative stress is accompanied by an adaptive tissue response involving increased activity of glutathione-dependent enzymes in liver; (iii) the observed changes are not accompanied by a better protection against oxidative stress in folate-repleted rats.
folate deficiency in rats causes oxidative stress, which is associated with changes in the activity of glutathione-dependent enzymes.
folate deficiency causes oxidative stress and that this is compensated by a preferential response of glutamine-related enzymes in the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the redox status and antioxidant capacity of rats in relation to folate intake.
the redox status and the antioxidant capacity in rats fed with folate-deficient diets.
the antioxidant properties of folates, and the possible consequences of their deficiency on the redox status in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the redox status is not a limiting factor of the preventive effect of folate on degenerative diseases.
a folate deficiency induces an adaptive tissue response that is not necessarily associated with a better protection against oxidative stress.
folate deficiency is associated with a better liver protection against oxidative stress, whereas folate supplementation is not associated with a better protection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the redox state in liver and heart is not affected by the folate status, but that the folate status affects the redox state and the antioxidant enzymes in liver.
folate deficiency is a condition that causes oxidative stress in adult rats, but the antioxidant response to folate deficiency is not a linear one.
the folate-dependent changes of redox status of rat liver are mainly due to changes of the glutathione-related pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antioxidant properties of folates may not be sufficient to counteract the deleterious effect of oxidative stress in folate deficiency.
folate deficiency induces a compensatory mechanism in the rat liver to counteract oxidative stress.
folate deficiency may induce oxidative stress and the antioxidant system may respond by increasing the activity of some of its components, including enzymes involved in glutathione metabolism.
